referents.why: 'his hand' (third masc sg possessive): Aaron, the subject of the stretching out
third feminine singular 'it covered': the frog (w12, feminine singular), the subject carried on from cl1
referents.category: third person with a feminine antecedent

links.why: then links only within a verse; the link from the earlier command is recorded as fulfilment below
the coming up of the frogs is what the stretching out brings about, so it is a result rather than a plain next event
Aaron stretched out the hand, and so the frogs came up: a clause stating what the act brings about (R4)
Aaron stretches out the hand he was commanded to stretch out; the same verb reports the command carried out
the frogs came up, the effect of the command to bring them up (same root, different stem)
a wayyiqtol continues the narrative line: the frogs covered the land after they came up
